1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — apply a downward bias correction of 3–8% depending on recent volatility.
2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 5–7 days post-spike.
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day average of true values is lower than forecast, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days backward in time for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
5. For 30-day forecasts, model ignores recent downward trends — if last 7 days show declining prices, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7 days.
6. Model overreacts to minor historical volatility — if recent 7-day range is narrow, reduce forecast variance by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.
